_readme: Every hand-off between two scenes the edit knows, and what calls for it. The chain is: the teardown's Layers column names a hand-off out of a scene ("transition out: whip") → the brief carries it as layers.transitions [{after_scene, kind}] → the edit draws it. When nothing is asked, it is a hard cut — the house default (cut on the line, sound leading). `drawn: true` rows the edit draws today; `drawn: false` rows are HyperFrames registry items worth having (registry ids listed, nothing installed) — the gate refuses them until they are. Those rows carry `state: "not installed"` beside their `status` (rule 6: status is draft / approved / deprecated only; the developer, triage page 15, 2026-10-07); the gate reads `drawn`. `type: move` is a move inside one shot, not a hand-off, and cannot be asked for in layers.transitions. Only the owner signs a row approved.

transitions.name: Hard cut
transitions.what: No transition. The next line starts over the tail of the last shot.
transitions.trigger: Nothing asked. A hard cut is what happens between every two scenes unless the plan's layers.transitions names something else for that scene.
transitions.when_to_use: Almost always. Talking-head ads cut on the line with the sound leading; any effect has to earn its place.

transitions.name: Punch in
transitions.what: Same shot, jumps 12% closer on the key word. Not a transition between clips — a move inside one.
transitions.trigger: Not asked for — the edit does it by itself: talking A-roll cut at a pause gets alternate cuts punched in 7% so the jump reads as a choice. A plan cannot ask for it in layers.transitions (the gate refuses it there).
transitions.when_to_use: Inside one talking clip, at a trimmed pause or on a key word.

transitions.name: Whip
transitions.what: The outgoing shot flicks sideways with motion blur and the next one lands from the other side. For 'and then' energy between two related shots.
transitions.registry: whip-pan (shader block — not installed; this is the CSS version)
transitions.trigger: The teardown's Layers column names the hand-off out of a scene ("transition out: whip") → the brief carries it as layers.transitions [{after_scene, kind: "whip"}] → the edit draws it.
transitions.when_to_use: 'And then' energy between two related shots; a quick jump in place or time.

transitions.name: Match cut
transitions.what: A hard cut on a shape or move the two shots share; the incoming shot starts at the outgoing shot's framing and settles, so the eye carries across. The match itself is made by the pictures.
transitions.trigger: The teardown's Layers column names the hand-off out of a scene ("transition out: match") → the brief carries it as layers.transitions [{after_scene, kind: "match"}] → the edit draws it. The two pictures must already share a shape or move — production makes that; the edit only carries the eye across.
transitions.when_to_use: Before/after on the same framing, product to product, hand to hand.

transitions.name: Zoom through
transitions.what: The outgoing shot pushes in fast with a blur; the next one arrives from slightly wide and settles. For a reveal or a jump in scale.
transitions.registry: cinematic-zoom (shader block — not installed; this is the CSS version)
transitions.trigger: The teardown's Layers column names the hand-off out of a scene ("transition out: zoom") → the brief carries it as layers.transitions [{after_scene, kind: "zoom"}] → the edit draws it.
transitions.when_to_use: A reveal or a jump in scale — into the product, into the mechanism.

transitions.name: Flash
transitions.what: Two frames of white between worlds — for a before/after or a show's replay.
transitions.registry: flash-through-white (shader block — not installed; this is the CSS version)
transitions.trigger: The teardown's Layers column names the hand-off out of a scene ("transition out: flash") → the brief carries it as layers.transitions [{after_scene, kind: "flash"}] → the edit draws it.
transitions.when_to_use: Between worlds: before/after, a replay, a memory, a camera-flash moment.

transitions.name: Whip pan (motion blur)
transitions.what: A full-frame whip with real directional motion blur — the better version of our CSS whip.
transitions.trigger: The teardown's Layers column names the hand-off out of a scene ("transition out: whip-pan-cut") → the brief carries it as layers.transitions [{after_scene, kind: "whip-pan-cut"}] → the edit draws it. Listed, NOT installed: the gate refuses it until someone installs the registry item and the edit learns to draw it.
transitions.when_to_use: When the CSS whip looks too clean.

transitions.trigger: The teardown's Layers column names the hand-off out of a scene ("transition out: cut-the-curve") → the brief carries it as layers.transitions [{after_scene, kind: "cut-the-curve"}] → the edit draws it. transitions.trigger: The teardown's Layers column names the hand-off out of a scene ("transition out: push") → the brief carries it as layers.transitions [{after_scene, kind: "push"}] → the edit draws it. transitions.trigger: The teardown's Layers column names the hand-off out of a scene ("transition out: scribble-wipe") → the brief carries it as layers.transitions [{after_scene, kind: "scribble-wipe"}] → the edit draws it. transitions.trigger: The teardown's Layers column names the hand-off out of a scene ("transition out: beat-freeze") → the brief carries it as layers.transitions [{after_scene, kind: "beat-freeze"}] → the edit draws it. transitions.name: Cube turn
transitions.what: The shot turns away on a cube face and the next face turns in, with a soft floor reflection.
transitions.trigger: The teardown's Layers column names the hand-off out of a scene ("transition out: gl-cube") → the brief carries it as layers.transitions [{after_scene, kind: "gl-cube"}] → the edit draws it: a WebGL pass over the two pictures, centred on the cut.
transitions.when_to_use: A chapter change: problem → solution, before → after, 'here's the thing'.

transitions.name: Directional warp
transitions.what: The next shot sweeps in diagonally, the old one stretching away along the same line.
transitions.trigger: The teardown's Layers column names the hand-off out of a scene ("transition out: gl-directional-warp") → the brief carries it as layers.transitions [{after_scene, kind: "gl-directional-warp"}] → the edit draws it: a WebGL pass over the two pictures, centred on the cut.
transitions.when_to_use: 'And then' energy with more push than the whip — a fast jump between related shots.

transitions.name: Pixelate
transitions.what: The frame breaks into squares at the midpoint and resolves into the next shot.
transitions.trigger: The teardown's Layers column names the hand-off out of a scene ("transition out: gl-pixelize") → the brief carries it as layers.transitions [{after_scene, kind: "gl-pixelize"}] → the edit draws it: a WebGL pass over the two pictures, centred on the cut.
transitions.when_to_use: A techy or gamey change of scene; 'glitch' in a screen-recording ad.

transitions.trigger: The teardown's Layers column names the hand-off out of a scene ("transition out: gl-zoom-blur") → the brief carries it as layers.transitions [{after_scene, kind: "gl-zoom-blur"}] → the edit draws it: a WebGL pass over the two pictures, centred on the cut.

transitions.name: Cross warp

transitions.trigger: The teardown's Layers column names the hand-off out of a scene ("transition out: gl-crosswarp") → the brief carries it as layers.transitions [{after_scene, kind: "gl-crosswarp"}] → the edit draws it: a WebGL pass over the two pictures, centred on the cut.

transitions.name: Doorway
transitions.what: The old shot splits down the middle like doors opening onto the next.
transitions.trigger: The teardown's Layers column names the hand-off out of a scene ("transition out: gl-doorway") → the brief carries it as layers.transitions [{after_scene, kind: "gl-doorway"}] → the edit draws it: a WebGL pass over the two pictures, centred on the cut.

transitions.what: The next shot pushes the old one up and off, like a feed scroll.
transitions.trigger: The teardown's Layers column names the hand-off out of a scene ("transition out: gl-push-up") → the brief carries it as layers.transitions [{after_scene, kind: "gl-push-up"}] → the edit draws it: a WebGL pass over the two pictures, centred on the cut.
